issue.title: test_real_zsh_zcompile_and_registration flakes under the full parallel lane: probe_zsh_comps' 5s interactive-zsh timeout returns None, so registered is None instead of True
issue.description:
tests/completion/test_install_zsh.py::test_real_zsh_zcompile_and_registration failed once under the whole-suite parallel lane and passes reliably standalone.

OBSERVATION: 2026-08-17T22:58Z, epic phase sase-p2.1 (project-scoped repo mention catalog, epic sase-p2). 'just check' ran every lint gate green and then the full test suite: 32553 passed, 1 failed, this node the only failure. An isolated re-run of the node passed. The diff under test was src/sase/xprompt/{repo_mention_catalog.py,glossary_catalog.py} plus tests — nothing touching shell completion, install, or zsh. The phase agent recorded it as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP; sase-p2.land is filing it.

LIKELY ROOT CAUSE (code path, not yet confirmed against a captured assertion): the test is the repo's only real-zsh test and its last assertion is 'assert result.registered is True'. That value comes from install_completion -> _verify_install (src/sase/completion/install.py:505-535), whose default probe is probe_zsh_comps (src/sase/completion/install_targets.py:282-308). probe_zsh_comps shells out to an INTERACTIVE zsh -- [zsh, '-ic', 'print -r -- ${_comps[sase]:-UNSET}'] -- with timeout=ZSH_PROBE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 5.0 (install_targets.py:21), and on subprocess.TimeoutExpired or OSError it returns None. _verify_install maps a None probe to (None, InstallStep('verify','skip','could not probe ${_comps[sase]}'), hint, verify_failed=False), so result.registered becomes None while result.ok stays True and exit_code stays 0. That is exactly the shape of an intermittent failure that only trips the 'registered is True' assertion: the three preceding assertions (result.ok, script.is_file(), zwc_path(script).is_file()) and the two following (registered, exit_code) would all still pass except 'registered is True'.

Under the full parallel lane this test pays for an interactive zsh startup that sources the fixture .zshrc and runs 'compinit -u' over the entire real fpath in a tmp HOME, competing with every xdist worker for CPU; 5.0s is a fixed wall-clock budget with no attempt bound, which is the classic profile for a load-only flake. This is a timing/wait defect, not process-global state leakage: the test builds its own ZDOTDIR, HOME, fpath, and zcompdump under tmp_path and shares no module-level state.

SCOPE: confirm the signature by capturing the assertion (rerun the node under deliberate CPU oversubscription, e.g. the harness pattern in 'just test-contention'), then either give the probe a bounded-retry/attempt-based wait instead of a single fixed 5s deadline, raise the probe budget for the test via the existing verify_fn seam, or make the test assert on a deterministic seam rather than a live interactive-zsh probe. Do not simply widen the constant for production use without evidence: 5s is a user-facing 'sase completion install' latency budget too.

REPRODUCTION COMMAND: '.venv/bin/python tools/run_pytest default tests/completion/test_install_zsh.py' passes standalone; the failure has only been seen inside the full parallel lane. Requires zsh on PATH (the module is skipped otherwise).

payload.entry: RELATED: sase-og — sibling load-only flake filed from the same epic (sase-p2.2). Same class (a fixed wall-clock wait that is not enough under the full parallel lane) but a different root cause and a different wait: sase-og is a pause(0.25) on an async modal collision check, this one is a 5.0s subprocess timeout on an interactive-zsh probe. Whoever fixes either should check whether tools/check_test_wait_helpers can be taught to catch the other's shape.

RELATED: sase-j7 — in-progress epic for the flake class rooted in process-global state leaking between tests. Recording the boundary explicitly: this node is NOT in that class. It builds its own ZDOTDIR, HOME, fpath, and zcompdump under tmp_path and shares no module-level state, so the fix belongs in the wait/probe budget rather than in test isolation.

evidence.note: Independent reproduction from closed epic phase sase-p3.15.3 (2026-08-18T23:06:49Z, workspace sase_12, epic sase-p3.15 required-plugin install repair), filed here by sase-p3.15.land. Signature matches this bead exactly: under the full parallel lane (14 xdist workers, 33773 collected items) the node asserted 'result.registered is True' and got None; 6/6 serial reruns on the same tree passed. The diff under test was sase/sase.yml plugins.required plus tools/setup_required_plugins -- no completion, install, or zsh files -- so it is not attributable to that change. This is the second independent sighting of the None-from-probe_zsh_comps shape described in the bead, on a different tree and a different epic, which supports the load-only-flake diagnosis over a real regression.

Independent reproduction from epic sase-qv landing. Phase bead sase-qv.1 (monitor status contract module) recorded this as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP on 2026-08-19T13:57:51Z: tests/completion/test_install_zsh.py::test_real_zsh_zcompile_and_registration failed once in an escalated parallel full suite with registered=None, then passed on a serial rerun of the same tree. The diff under test was src/sase/monitor_status.py + src/sase/palette_hash.py and monitor read paths -- nothing touching shell completion, install, or zsh -- so this is a second, independent confirmation of the probe_zsh_comps 5s interactive-zsh timeout mechanism this bead already describes. Impact: the node is the only failure and turns check-full red for an unrelated diff.

Assertion: result.registered is True got None (InstallResult.ok=True, exit_code=0 — the probe_zsh_comps timeout shape). Serial rerun of tests/completion/test_install_zsh.py::test_real_zsh_zcompile_and_registration on the same tree passed in 2.02s. Diff under test is LLM usage-limit matching/disable (claude.py, usage_limit_config.py, run_agent_exec_retry.py) — nothing touching completion, install, or zsh.

Independent reproduction from closed epic phase sase-qv.8.1 (2026-08-19). just check lint was green; the Justfile justfile-rule escalation ran the full lane: 34715 passed / 1 failed. Failure: tests/completion/test_install_zsh.py::test_real_zsh_zcompile_and_registration with InstallResult.registered is None. Isolation rerun on the same tree passed in 2.02s with -p no:randomly. Unrelated to dismissed-archive wait resolution (sase-qv.8.1 only touched src/sase/core/dismissed_agent_completion.py and its tests). Matches the existing diagnosis: probe_zsh_comps 5s interactive-zsh timeout returns None under the full parallel lane.
